sample_unit: patient planning CT scans (859 clinically approved contours)

links.outcome: Commercial AI autocontour agreement with clinically approved contours on local multi-clinic CT data
links.effect: High agreement (DSC >0.9) in 27.8%, 32.8%, 34.1% of cases; low agreement (DSC <0.5) in 7.4%, 8.8%, 6.1%; worse in brain and H&N than pelvis and thorax.
links.quote: All 3 solutions had low quantitative agreement in 7.4%, 8.8%, and 6.1% of cases (DSC <0.5), performing worse in brain (median DSC = 0.65/0.78/0.75) and H&N (median DSC = 0.76/0.80/0.81).

links.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of three commercial autocontouring products on same patient data
links.effect: AI1/AI2/AI3 differed by disease site; e.g., brain median DSC 0.65/0.78/0.75; qualitative acceptability 70.7% (AI1) and 74.6% (AI2) of ROIs.
links.quote: Qualitatively, AI1 and AI2 contours were acceptable (rated 1-2) with at most minor edits in 70.7% and 74.6% of ROIs (2906 ratings), higher for abdomen (AI1: 79.2%) and thorax (AI2: 90.2%), and lower for H&N (29.0/35.6%).

links.outcome: Blinded expert clinician Likert ratings of AI-generated contours
links.effect: Multiple experts rated blinded AI contours; 70.7% (AI1) and 74.6% (AI2) of ROIs acceptable with at most minor edits across 2906 ratings; H&N lower (29.0/35.6%).
links.quote: Qualitative assessment was performed by multiple experts scoring blinded AI-contours using a Likert scale.

links.outcome: End-user workflow and usability survey of autocontouring solutions
links.effect: Survey showed strong user preference for full automation and mixed preferences for accuracy versus total number of structures generated.
links.quote: An end-user survey showed strong user preference for full automation and mixed preferences for accuracy versus total number of structures generated.

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating three commercial AI autocontouring tools using a multi-clinic validation framework assessing quantitative metrics, qualitative expert review, and workflow/usability.
